memoryText: But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 2 Peter 3:18 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
These are Peter’s last written words, and they are a command to keep growing. After warnings about false teachers and scoffers, his remedy is not only to guard but to grow. A healthy plant resists disease. A Christian who grows in grace and knowledge is harder to lead astray.

Grace comes first. We grow in the grace of God, receiving more of his kindness and being shaped by it. Knowledge comes second: not just information, but knowing Christ more deeply. The two go together; knowledge without grace puffs up, and grace without knowledge stays shallow.

Notice the object: “our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.” Growth is growth toward and into him. And the verse ends with praise: “To him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity.” Our growth is for his glory. Ask the Lord today where he wants you to grow.
weekInReview: This week you read the rest of 1 Peter and all of 2 Peter. First Peter 2 and 3 called us to honor everyone, follow the example of Christ who bore our sins on the tree, and always be ready to explain our hope with gentleness and respect. First Peter 4 and 5 taught us to love earnestly, use our gifts as good stewards, not be surprised by fiery trials, shepherd willingly, cast our anxieties on God, resist the roaring lion, and trust the God of all grace. Second Peter 1 told us that God has given us everything we need for life and godliness and urged us to add virtue to our faith. On Day 851 we paused on the origin and canon of Scripture. Second Peter 2 and 3 warned us about false teachers and scoffers and pointed to the patience of the Lord and the new heavens and new earth. Psalm 34 invited us to taste and see that the LORD is good.
reflectionQuestions: Peter says to be ready to give a defense for the hope that is in you with gentleness and respect. What is your hope, and how would you explain it in two minutes to a neighbor who asked?
Peter says to cast all your anxieties on God because he cares for you. What anxiety are you carrying right now? What would it look like to hand it to him in prayer today?
Peter’s final words are to grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. In what area do you most want to grow in the next month, and what is one practical step?
prayerPrompts: Thank God for rest and for his word.
Ask him to help you grow in grace and knowledge.
